t: Hollywood Rocks 'n' Rolls in the '50s
d: This movie is a look at the birth of Rock ‘n’ Roll and how Hollywood captured it on film. Listen, and learn, as a top music historian gives his insights on the artists and movies that have become an integral part of the Fabulous 50s.

t: Magic Encounters: Episode 1
d: In the area around the Cape of Good Hope Andreas Kieling finds opportunities both on land and under water to experience thrilling adventures in the pursuit of his profession.

t: Magic Encounters: Episode 2
d: In this, Part 2 of the series, Kieling again travels to exotic countries. This time he is searching for the last example of various species in Indonesia, Canada and Rwanda.

t: Cowboy Country
d: Beginning in the early 1840's, more than 350,000 emigrants headed out into the American West in covered wagons, on horseback and on foot. It was one of the biggest migrations in human history and one of the most difficult.

t: Cowboy Country
d: For centuries, the native peoples of the American West lived a proud, independent life. But in the mid of the 19th century they found themselves overwhelmed by a torrent of emigrants.

t: Cowboy Country
d: Hollywood's portrayal of the American West may not always have been accurate but it's certainly helped preserve interest in this colorful or American history.

t: Cowboy Country
d: More than liberty, land or lumber, gold paved the way for the settlement of the American West.

t: Cowboy Country
d: Nothing so fundamentally changed the American West as did the "iron horse." This new form of transportation created fortunes, hastened the end of ancient cultures and shaped a new world.

t: Cowboy Country
d: The history of the American West is often most colorfully told in places like Tombstone, Arizona; South Pass City, Wyoming; and Deadwood, South Dakota.

t: Notorious Women Of The Bible: Eve – The Original Rebel
d: The story of Eve opens up with a vision of loneliness, companionship, desire and love. It tells she, gives up a life of ease in an idyllic setting, along with the promise of immortality, and instead chooses to pursue wisdom and intimacy with her man.

t: Notorious Women Of The Bible: Delilah – One Feisty Femme
d: Samson may have been the classic biblical Israeli strong man, but he was no match for a pretty young Philistine named Delilah. We all think we know this traditional tale, but do we? Was Delilah a pawn, a Judas or a survivor?

t: Notorious Women Of The Bible: Bathsheba – Wife, Mother, Queen
d: A late afternoon in Jerusalem. A beautiful young woman bathes on the roof under the last rays of dusk, espied by the lustful eyes of a hidden admirer. The admirer, King David, is not where he’s supposed to be, on the battlefield with his troops.

t: Notorious Women Of The Bible: Jezebel – The Ultimate Bad Girl
d: No biblical woman is more reviled than Jezebel. Her name lives to this day as a synonym for feminine evil. Jezebel’s story is a rich mix of historical events, allegorical interpretation and metaphorical license.

t: Notorious Women Of The Bible: Esther – A Clever Heroine
d: The book of Esther tells the story of a beautiful orphan who hides her Jewish identity, becomes Queen of Persia and saves her people. A controversial figure, Esther has been criticized for being a ‘bad Jew’ and being vengeful and bloodthirsty.

t: 100 Years of Comedy
d: A history of 100 years of comedy from slapstick silent films, screwball comedies of the 1930s and '40s, and the red hot hi-jinks of Hollywood's most recent comedies!

t: Greatest Crimes of All Time: Woman Killers
d: Ted Bundy – maybe the most famous Woman Killer. But there are more. Ant they all create a perfect social environment in which no one recognizes their true nature.

t: Greatest Crimes of All Time: Ruthless Killers
d: Ruthless Killers: They kill for all manner of reasons. Their victims: men, women, and even children. What motivates them, and how can they be stopped? Investigators reach their limits hunting them down.

t: Greatest Crimes of All Time: Angels of Death
d: In hospitals and nursing wards, death is an everyday occurrence. And that is precisely what they count on: angels of death. Some of them rack up more victims in this way than the worst serial killers in the world.

t: Greatest Crimes of All Time: Gang Bosses
d: They rule the underworld: gang bosses. They make millions with racketeering and drug trafficking. For investigators, it is more than a fight against criminality – it is a veritable war.

t: Greatest Crimes of All Time: Bank Robbers
d: Bank robbers. They are clever, planning their crimes for years. And if necessary, they even put human lives at risk. For investigators, each heist is different. But all robbers have one thing in common: they steal millions.

t: Greatest Crimes of All Time: Rampage Killers
d: Rampage Killers. They come out of nowhere – and when they occur, innocent people always die. Investigators must react in a flash and make difficult decisions.  Every killing spree is a race against time.

t: Greatest Crimes of All Time: Female Murderers
d: Women usually kill in their own peculiar way: sophisticated, tactically, and from behind. They prefer tainted medicines, knives, or poison. And they often kill for years, unnoticed and in secret.

t: Greatest Crimes of All Time: Serial Killers
d: Serial Killers victims are often selected at random. The murders have only one thing in common: the bodies are savagely disfigured. Hunting them leads investigators into a world of darkness.
